newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Property sales drive New World interim.
newsitem.headline: Property sales drive New World interim.

text.p: Strong property sales drove growth of New World Development Co Ltd's interim profits announced on Tuesday, and the company said it remained confident in the market's prospects.
New World reported net profit of HK$2.2 billion for the six months to December 31, up 29 percent from HK$1.7 billion in the year-ago period.
The strong performance was derived chiefly from the positive trend in Hong Kong's residential property market during the past 12 months.

"I myself definitely have full confidence in the property market in Hong Kong, mainly because I believe there is very strong demand...for residential units," managing director Henry Cheng said at a news conference on Tuesday.
He added the company has applied to the government for permission to develop ten properties owned by the company and currently zoned as farmland into residential developments.
In all these sites would give the group a future developable landbank of 11.3 million sq ft, Cheng said.
Operation profit derived from sales of new properties rose to HK$796.6 million, an 324.4 percent increase over HK$187.7 million recorded in the year-earlier period.
During the period, the company sold Phase I of Discovery Park, a large residential development in which the group has a 50 percent stake, at an average HK$5,048 per sq ft.

It also brought to market the extension to its Telford Gardens development, a multi-use building in which the company also has a 50 percent stake. The average sale price of the Kowloon property was HK$4,870 per sq ft.
In all, property sales accounted for 34.1 percent of total operating profit during the period.

The group's large portfolio of rental properties was the next largest contributor. Operating profit from the company's 4.65 million sq ft of commercial properties was HK$692.7 million, a 7.5 percent increase over the corresponding period last year to account for 30.9 percent of the total.
The New World Hotel group achieved a strong 25.5 percent rise in operating profit to HK$658.5 million, to account for 29.3 percent of the total.

The group owns and manages four hotels in Hong Kong, including the five-star Regent Hotel and Grand Hyatt Hotel. In addition it owns minority stakes in six hotels in China, which it also manages. It also has minority holdings in hotels in Vietnam, the Philippines and Malaysia.
The company is also the owner of the Ramada Renaissance Hotel group, with nine hotels in North America, France and Australia.
The "others" category, however, showed an increasing loss of HK$117.3 million against HK$12.3 million last year.
Besides properties, hotels and infrastructure, New World is involved in telecommunications, department stores and several other areas.

Subsidiary New World Infrastructure Ltd, which is 62.92 percent held by the parent company, reported net profit of HK$273.42 million for the fiscal year's first six months, a 28.0 percent increase from last year.

The unit's contribution to the New World Development at the operating profit level was HK$92.8 million, a 10.6 percent increase. In all the infrastructure arm contributed HK$172.03 million to the bottom line including profits from joint ventures in China.
